title: Proper base change on classical pro-étale complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of
schemes, and let $g:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary. Set $X'=X\times_YY'$, with
projections $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$. If
$K\in D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ has torsion underlying
abelian cohomology sheaves, the canonical exchange, defined as in
[sk-def-exchange] from the pro-étale inverse and direct images $g^*,g'^*$ and
$Rf_*,Rf'_*$ on $D^+(\,\cdot_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$,

$$
g^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf'_*g'^*K
$$

is an isomorphism in $D^+_{\mathrm{class}}(Y'_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$.

The complex $K$ need not be constructible, and the torsion orders need not be
invertible on $Y$. Classicality of $K$ is required: it is what brings the
statement back to the étale site.

proof.text: Put $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for each corner $T$. The bounded-below unit is an isomorphism for our discrete commutative ring by [sk-prop-sf-comparison], so the hypothesis of [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence] holds. Set $L=R\nu_{X,*}K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Its counit gives a specified isomorphism $\alpha:A_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. The exactness of $A_X$ on module sheaves in [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] and the cohomology identity in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] give $A_XH^q(L)\simeq H^q(K)$ for every $q$. All coefficients here are discrete constant rings.

source.place: Opening paragraph and Stacks Tag 099V (lemma-relative-comparison): descend via the existing arbitrary-ring classical equivalence

proof.text: The etale complex $L$ has torsion underlying abelian cohomology. Indeed fix $F=H^q(L)$ and let $c_F:\operatorname{colim}_nF[n]\to F$ be the canonical map, with positive integers ordered by divisibility, as in [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. The same local-torsion condition on the pro-etale site is the assertion that $\operatorname{colim}_nG[n]\to G$ is invertible for $G=H^q(K)$; this is a sheaf colimit, not a bound on all sections of an object. The exact, fully faithful left adjoint $A_X$ of [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] preserves $F[n]=\ker(n:F\to F)$ and, by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], its filtered colimit. Colimits and kernels of module sheaves have the corresponding underlying abelian colimits and kernels by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Hence $A_X(c_F)$ identifies with $c_{H^q(K)}$, an isomorphism by hypothesis. Full faithfulness reflects isomorphisms: lift the inverse of $A_X(c_F)$ and use faithfulness to check both inverse identities. Thus $c_F$ is invertible, which is exactly torsion for the underlying etale abelian sheaf. No integer annihilating all of $F$ has been chosen.

source.place: Opening paragraph: torsion reflection from exactness, full faithfulness and adjunction; elementary assembly of cited statements

proof.text: Work first with a torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ placed in degree zero. The given proper $f$ and arbitrary $g$ satisfy exactly the hypotheses of [lemma-weil-pbc-torsion-assembly]; it asserts that the specified derived exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,F}$ is an isomorphism. This is the sheaf-level input supplied by the projective-line, proper-morphism reduction and torsion-assembly route of this unit. It includes all primes, including residue characteristics.

source.place: Opening paragraph; Stacks Tag 095T (theorem-proper-base-change): etale torsion-sheaf input

proof.text: Let $E\in D^+(X_{\Et})$ be an abelian complex with torsion cohomology and fix $a$ such that $H^q(E)=0$ for $q<a$. Put $E_b=\tau_{\leq b}E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $E_{a-1}$ has zero cohomology, so it is the zero object by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology], applied to $0\to E_{a-1}$. The two triangulated functors preserve zero objects, so the exchange at zero is the unique morphism between zero objects and is invertible. Induct for $b\geq a$ using the distinguished triangle $E_{b-1}\to E_b\to H^b(E)[-b]\to E_{b-1}[1]$ of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle]. Both $\Phi=g^{-1}Rf_*$ and $\Psi=Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ are triangulated functors $D^+(X_{\Et})\to D^+(Y'_{\Et})$, as composites of the triangulated inverse images of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and the triangulated derived direct images of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated], with the composite shift isomorphisms $\xi,\zeta$; so they carry the truncation triangle to distinguished triangles, as [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] requires. The exchange is compatible with these shift isomorphisms, $\zeta\circ\Ex_{\square,M[1]}=\Ex_{\square,M}[1]\circ\xi$, by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated] (1), iterated for all shifts. Its component at $H^b(E)[-b]$ is therefore invertible by step 3, and its component at $E_{b-1}$ is invertible by induction. The two-out-of-three statement [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] makes its component at $E_b$ invertible. Thus the exchange is invertible at every bounded upper truncation, by finite induction.

source.place: Bounded-below paragraph; Stacks Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle): finite Postnikov induction

proof.text: For the same $E$ and any integer $m$, let $c_m:E_m\to E$ be the canonical truncation. The categories of abelian etale sheaves are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck], and $f_*,f'_*$ are left exact additive functors by [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-left-exact]; their bounded-below right derived functors are the K-injective ones of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso] applies. It gives an isomorphism on $H^m$ for $Rf_*(c_m)$, and exactness of $g^{-1}$ ([prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]) gives one for $g^{-1}Rf_*(c_m)$. For the other side, $g'^{-1}(c_m)$ is an isomorphism on $H^i$ for $i\leq m$ and a monomorphism on $H^{m+1}$: exact inverse image preserves cohomology, and $H^{m+1}(E_m)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology]. Apply the general morphism clause of the same truncation lemma with $v=f'_*$ to get an isomorphism on $H^m$ for $Rf'_*g'^{-1}(c_m)$. Naturality of the exchange ([sk-def-exchange]) makes the square with these vertical maps commute. Its top component at $E_m$ is invertible by step 4 (or $E_m=0$ if $m<a$); hence $H^m(\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,E})$ is invertible. Since $m$ is arbitrary, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology] makes $\operatorname{Ex}_{\square,E}$ invertible in $D^+(Y'_{\Et})$. This argument never takes a limit of an unbounded Postnikov tower.

source.place: Bounded-below paragraph; Stacks Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), part (2) and proof: degreewise truncation comparison

proof.text: Return to the etale $\Lambda$-module complex $L$ of steps 1-2, and write $U$ for forgetting its module action. The exact forgetful functor has $H^q(UL)=UH^q(L)$, so $UL$ satisfies step 5. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]: its clauses (1) and (2) identify the inverse images and both derived direct images after forgetting, and clause (3) identifies $U(\operatorname{Ex}^{\Lambda}_{\square,L})$ with the specified abelian exchange at $UL$. Its final assertion reflects invertibility. Hence the etale module exchange $E_L:l_gr_fL\to r_{f'}l_{g'}L$ is invertible, where $l_u=u_{\Et}^{-1}$ and $r_u=Ru_{\Et,*}$. This uses acyclicity under forgetting, rather than asserting that forgetting preserves injectives.

The base change $f'$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Properness includes finite type and separatedness by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; finite type includes quasi-compactness by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and a separated morphism is quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Consequently $f$ and $f'$ are qcqs, with no quasi-compactness assumption on any base scheme or on $g$. Write $p_u=u_{\Proet}^*$ and $s_u=Ru_{\Proet,*}$ with discrete constant coefficients. By [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], choose the canonical inverse-image comparisons $a_u:A_{\operatorname{source}(u)}l_u\xrightarrow{\sim}p_uA_{\operatorname{target}(u)}$ for all four edges, using the inverse orientation of its displayed comparison, and its direct-image comparisons $b_u:A_{\operatorname{target}(u)}r_u\xrightarrow{\sim}s_uA_{\operatorname{source}(u)}$ for $u=f,f'$. They respect units, counits and composition. Define the endpoint isomorphisms
$$S_L=p_g(b_{f,L})\circ a_{g,r_fL}:A_{Y'}l_gr_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}p_gs_fA_XL,$$
$$T_L=s_{f'}(a_{g',L})\circ b_{f',l_{g'}L}:A_{Y'}r_{f'}l_{g'}L\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{f'}p_{g'}A_XL.$$
In particular the comparison for $g:Y'\to Y$ uses $A_{Y'}$, not $A_X$.

source.place: Pro-etale paragraph: qcqs vertical edges and the canonical comparison maps; arbitrary-discrete-ring comparison as stated in sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison

proof.text:
Check the arrow under these comparisons. Write the etale exchange as $E_L=e_3e_2e_1$, where $e_1$ inserts the unit of $l_{f'}\dashv r_{f'}$, $e_2$ is $r_{f'}$ applied to the inverse-image square $l_{f'}l_g\simeq l_{g'}l_f$, and $e_3=r_{f'}l_{g'}(\varepsilon_f)$; this is exactly [sk-def-exchange]. Write the pro-etale exchange $E^p_{A_XL}=p_3p_2p_1$ by the same unit--square--counit formula in [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-three-step-adjunction-comparison] to the four $A_T$ and the $a_u,b_f,b_{f'}$ of step 7. Its unit/counit hypotheses are the unit/counit compatibility in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]; its pullback cube is the compatibility with composition there, applied to the equality $fg'=gf'$. Here the intermediate etale vertices are $r_{f'}l_{f'}l_gr_fL$ and $r_{f'}l_{g'}l_fr_fL$, and the pro-etale vertices are $s_{f'}p_{f'}p_gs_fA_XL$ and $s_{f'}p_{g'}p_fs_fA_XL$. The cited three-step lemma states only that there exist four vertex isomorphisms, $V_0:A_{Y'}l_gr_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}p_gs_fA_XL$, $V_1:A_{Y'}r_{f'}l_{f'}l_gr_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{f'}p_{f'}p_gs_fA_XL$, $V_2:A_{Y'}r_{f'}l_{g'}l_fr_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{f'}p_{g'}p_fs_fA_XL$ and $V_3:A_{Y'}r_{f'}l_{g'}L\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{f'}p_{g'}A_XL$, with $V_1A_{Y'}(e_1)=p_1V_0$, $V_2A_{Y'}(e_2)=p_2V_1$ and $V_3A_{Y'}(e_3)=p_3V_2$ (compositions read right to left). Its proof builds them from the comparisons of step 7, but only their existence is used here. Composing the three squares gives
$$V_3\circ A_{Y'}(E_L)=E^p_{A_XL}\circ V_0.$$
Thus the specified pro-etale exchange at $A_XL$ is $V_3\circ A_{Y'}(E_L)\circ V_0^{-1}$, an isomorphism because $E_L$ is invertible by step 6, $A_{Y'}$ is a functor, and $V_0,V_3$ are isomorphisms. No finiteness hypothesis on $\Lambda$ was used; in particular the finite-ring statement of lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange is not being applied here.

source.place: Pro-etale paragraph; Stacks Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change), with unit/counit normalization of Tag 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints): compose the three comparison squares

proof.text: Use naturality of the exchange transformation of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] along $\alpha:A_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ from step 1: its component at $K$ is obtained from its component at $A_XL$ by the isomorphisms $p_gs_f(\alpha)$ and $s_{f'}p_{g'}(\alpha)$. Hence it too is invertible. Finally both endpoints are bounded below and classical. Indeed $r_fL$, $l_gr_fL$, $l_{g'}L$ and $r_{f'}l_{g'}L$ lie in the indicated bounded-below etale module categories by [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] and the exact inverse images in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. The functors $A_T$ carry them into the bounded-below classical subcategories by [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence] (whose unit hypothesis is supplied on each corner by [sk-prop-sf-comparison]). The maps $S_L,T_L$ and the isomorphism $\alpha$ identify them with the two pro-etale endpoints. Since the classical subcategory is full, the inverse of the exchange is a morphism in it. This proves exactly the isomorphism asserted in the statement.
